```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  warning = FALSE,
  dpi = 96,
  fig.align = "center",
  out.width = "100%"
)
source(file.path("..", "..", "pkgdown", "validation-helpers.R"))
bundle <- load_validation_bundle()
counts <- bundle$manifest$counts
```

RSYC yield curves were validated against independent ground plots from
`r bundle$manifest$validation$reference`. Each curve was compared with the
plots located in its tile or ecological unit. Plots were grouped into
`r bundle$manifest$validation$age_class_width`-year age classes, and plots
older than 150 years were excluded. For each age class, the weighted mean of
the plot observations and its
`r scales::percent(bundle$manifest$validation$ci_level)` confidence interval
(CI) were compared with the mean RSYC prediction for the same plots.

These results describe model release **`r bundle$version`**:
`r format(counts$validated_models, big.mark = ",")` of
`r format(counts$models, big.mark = ",")` published curves had enough plots
to validate. The remaining curves could not be validated because too few
suitable plots were available in their area.

Validation results are presented in three ways:

- this page summarises results across all models;
- [Validation by model group](validation-model-groups.html) shows
  scatterplots and errors by age for each response, scale, and spatial level;
- the [Validation explorer](validation-explorer.html) maps the results and
  shows the validation data for individual curves.

## Reliability tiers

Each validated curve was assigned a reliability tier based on its agreement
with the plot data. Curves with too few plots or age classes are marked as
having insufficient evidence.

```{r tiers, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 4.5, fig.alt = "Stacked bars showing the share of validated models in each reliability tier by response, scale, and spatial level."}
validation_tier_plot(bundle)
```

## Summary statistics

Statistics are calculated for each curve from its age-class means and then
summarised across curves. Bias is the mean difference between the RSYC
prediction and the observed plot mean, so positive values mean the curve
overestimates the plots. *Inside CI* is the share of age classes where the
mean prediction falls inside the 95% CI of the observed mean.

```{r summary-table}
validation_summary_table(bundle) %>%
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 1, 1, 0))
```

## Agreement with the plot confidence intervals

The proportion of curves whose prediction falls inside the plot CI, by age
class and spatial level. Panel labels give the overall proportion for each
level (EZ = ecozone, EP = ecoprovince, ER = ecoregion, ED = ecodistrict).
Only species validated at all five levels are shown.

```{r ci-coverage, results = "asis"}
for (y_var in names(response_names)) {
  cat("###", response_names[[y_var]], "{.tabset}\n\n")
  for (scale in names(scale_labels)) {
    cat("####", scale_labels[[scale]], "\n\n")
    p <- validation_ci_coverage(bundle, y_var, scale)
    knit_figure(
      p,
      height = figure_height(attr(p, "n_panels"), 1.4, 5.5) + 1,
      alt = sprintf(
        "Proportion of %s %s predictions inside the plot confidence interval by age class and spatial level, one panel per model.",
        response_names[[y_var]], scale
      )
    )
  }
}
```
